Name: PasswordBackup
Description: Configures where LAPS backs up the local admin password. Value 2 = Active Directory, ensuring centralized secure storage.
Security Impact: Not backing up to AD means local admin passwords are not centrally managed or recoverable.
Change Risk Level: High - Password backup location is critical; changing from AD breaks centralized password management.

Name: PasswordComplexity
Description: Sets the complexity requirements for LAPS-generated passwords. Value 4 = large letters, small letters, numbers, and special characters.
Security Impact: Lowering complexity reduces password strength, increasing brute-force vulnerability.
Change Risk Level: Medium - Lower complexity weakens local admin account security.

Name: PasswordLength
Description: Sets the minimum length for LAPS-generated passwords. Baseline requires 15+ characters.
Security Impact: Shorter passwords are easier to crack; 15 characters provides strong protection against brute-force.
Change Risk Level: Medium - Reducing length weakens password security proportionally.

Name: PassphraseLength
Description: Sets the minimum length for LAPS-generated passphrases (word-based passwords). Baseline requires 6+ words.
Security Impact: Shorter passphrases reduce entropy and are more susceptible to dictionary attacks.
Change Risk Level: Low - Passphrase length is a secondary control if password mode is used.

Name: PasswordAge
Description: Sets the maximum age in days for LAPS-managed passwords before automatic rotation. Baseline allows 30-365 days.
Security Impact: Longer rotation periods increase the window of exposure if a password is compromised.
Change Risk Level: Medium - Balance between security (shorter) and operational burden (longer).

Name: PostAuthActions
Description: Configures actions after the LAPS-managed account authenticates: reset password, logoff, reboot. Value 3 = reset password + reboot.
Security Impact: Weaker post-auth actions leave the rotated-out password valid longer than necessary.
Change Risk Level: Medium - Post-auth actions ensure compromised credentials are invalidated promptly.

Name: PostAuthGracePeriod
Description: Sets the grace period (in hours) after authentication before post-authentication actions are triggered. Baseline allows 8-24 hours.
Security Impact: Longer grace periods delay password rotation after use, extending exposure window.
Change Risk Level: Low - Grace period balances security with operational usability.

Name: AdminAccountName
Description: Specifies which local administrator account LAPS manages. If null, manages the built-in Administrator (RID 500).
Security Impact: Misconfiguring the account name causes LAPS to manage the wrong account or no account.
Change Risk Level: Medium - Must point to the correct local admin account; misconfiguration breaks LAPS management.

Name: PasswordEncryption
Description: Enables encryption of LAPS passwords stored in Active Directory. Requires Windows Server 2016+ domain functional level.
Security Impact: Disabling stores passwords in cleartext in AD, readable by any account with read access to the attribute.
Change Risk Level: High - Password encryption is critical; cleartext storage in AD is a severe security risk.

Name: AuthorizedDecryptors
Description: Specifies which principals can decrypt LAPS-encrypted passwords in AD. Controls access to local admin credentials.
Security Impact: Misconfiguring decryptors can lock out password recovery or grant access to unauthorized principals.
Change Risk Level: Medium - Access control for encrypted passwords; misconfiguration affects recoverability.

Name: EncryptedPasswordHistory
Description: Sets the number of encrypted password history entries stored in AD. Baseline allows 0-12.
Security Impact: History enables recovery of previous passwords if needed; too many increases storage and exposure.
Change Risk Level: Low - Password history is a recoverability feature; minimal security impact.

Name: ExpirationProtection
Description: Enables protection against password expiration tampering, ensuring LAPS-managed passwords are rotated on schedule.
Security Impact: Disabling allows manipulation of password expiration timestamps, preventing automatic rotation.
Change Risk Level: Medium - Ensures passwords are rotated even if expiration metadata is tampered with.

Name: AutoAccountManagement
Description: Controls whether LAPS automatically creates and manages the local administrator account. Baseline sets to disabled (0).
Security Impact: Enabling auto-management creates accounts automatically; may conflict with existing account provisioning.
Change Risk Level: Medium - Account auto-creation may conflict with existing account management processes.

Name: AutoAccountTarget
Description: Specifies the target for automatic account management: 0 = built-in admin, 1 = new managed account.
Security Impact: Controls whether LAPS manages the built-in admin or creates a separate managed account.
Change Risk Level: Low - Account target selection; depends on organizational account management strategy.

Name: AutoAccountName
Control Name: Enforce automatic account name or prefix
Description: Specifies the name or prefix for automatically managed LAPS accounts. Default: WLapsAdmin.
Security Impact: Name choice affects discoverability; predictable names may be targeted by attackers.
Change Risk Level: Low - Account naming convention; minimal security impact.

Name: AutoAccountRandomize
Description: Controls whether the automatically managed account name is randomized to prevent predictable targeting.
Security Impact: Non-randomized names are predictable and can be targeted in brute-force attacks.
Change Risk Level: Low - Name randomization is a minor defense-in-depth measure.

Name: AutoAccountEnable
Description: Controls whether the automatically created LAPS-managed account is enabled. Baseline sets to disabled (0).
Security Impact: Enabling creates an active local admin account that increases the attack surface.
Change Risk Level: Medium - Unnecessary enabled admin accounts increase attack surface.
